name: Jonadab
title: The Ancestor and Advisor of the Rechabites
summary: Jonadab, son of Rekab, was an influential figure in Israel's history known for two very different roles. In 2 Samuel, a Jonadab appears as Amnon's cunning advisor, while Jonadab son of Rekab in 2 Kings is known for his zeal for the Lord and for establishing the Rechabites' strict rules of conduct, which were praised by the prophet Jeremiah.

keyEvents.title: Jonadab's Advice to Amnon
keyEvents.description: Jonadab, son of Shimeah and David's nephew, gave the cunning advice to Amnon on how he could lure Tamar to him, which led to a terrible crime.

keyEvents.title: Jonadab Explains the Murder of Amnon
keyEvents.description: After Absalom killed Amnon, Jonadab explained to King David that only Amnon had been killed, not all the king's sons.

keyEvents.title: Jonadab Joins Jehu
keyEvents.description: Jonadab son of Rekab met King Jehu and joined him in his campaign against Baal worship in Israel, and they went together into Samaria.

keyEvents.title: The Extermination of the Baal Worshipers
keyEvents.description: Together with Jehu, Jonadab participated in the dramatic extermination of Baal's prophets and followers in Samaria, and Baal's temple was torn down.

keyEvents.title: The Rules of Life for the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: Jonadab son of Rekab established strict rules of life for his descendants: they were not to drink wine, not to build houses, not to sow seed or plant vineyards, but to live in tents.

keyEvents.title: God Praises the Faithfulness of the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah used the Rechabites' obedience to Jonadab's commands as an example and contrast to Israel's disobedience to God. The Lord promised that Jonadab's line would always have a man to stand before His presence.
